requirements.requirement: Provide an encrypted volume mounted at /srv/secure on node1.
requirements.summary: A valid LUKS2 container was created, opened as /dev/mapper/secure, formatted with XFS, and directly observed mounted at /srv/secure with readable test data. The same encrypted mapper, mount, and data were present after reboot.

requirements.requirement: The encrypted volume must unlock and mount automatically at boot.
requirements.summary: Crypttab and fstab generated the required systemd units. A bounded reboot changed the boot ID, after which the system was running, both encryption and mount units were active, data remained readable, and the boot journal directly recorded automatic unlocking followed by mounting.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes are satisfied. The evidence directly demonstrates an encrypted XFS volume mounted at /srv/secure and a successful reboot transition with automatic unlock, mount, preserved data, and no failed units. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for node1, and its boot identities agree with the fixed lifecycle observations.
limitations: Lifecycle snapshots are bounded and do not inventory the retained /etc backup files; their persistence is inferred from their successful creation and the absence of any later cleanup command.

operational_hygiene.summary: Implementation mutations were otherwise task-related: installing cryptsetup, creating and securing the key and backing container, configuring the filesystem and boot units, testing recovery, and rebooting. The only unnecessary retained mutation identified was creation of /etc/crypttab.pre-secure and /etc/fstab.pre-secure backup files; no cleanup removed them after successful validation. This is minor residual clutter. Post-execution checks show no failed services, no new listening exposure, and healthy package management.
